items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: Jack Teegarden was playing with Benny Pollock.

ctx.x: by the name of Jack Pettis, and we used to run across Louis every once in a while, you know. We'll be back on jazz review after this word. Now, a few words about the Sony 250A tape deck. Forget it. Forget about leaving it on. much about the Ellington band at the Cotton Club? Yeah, I used to go up there quite a bit because at that time everything was in Harlem. You know, there wasn't anything. They had big clubs downtown, but there was no jazz downtown in New York at all, and everything was in Harlem. And Jack Teegarden was playing with Benny Pollock. items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Pollock's band' and 'Benny Goodman and all those guys were with Pollock' in the context of discussing an arranger's work, but does not describe a personal relationship or direct collaboration with Benny Pollock himself.

ctx.x: Was it good or is it funny?

It was marvelous Bill, but it was the stinkinest tone, it was like Fazola playing the saxophone. Fazola was the world's worst sounding saxophone player that you ever heard in your life. In fact, cause Benny Pollock, two or three times, well not only Pollock, but Miller. And a lot of the band wanted him to play the lead, cause Fazola was a marvelous musician, you know. I mean he read the seven clefs and all. But man, the tone he got out of the saxophone, the sound of Sidney Ironman, the same Rapolo was the same…
But what about Snoozer? You were going to tell about how?
